author: potuz
content: Again the problem is not Prysm's timeout, that timeout shouldn't even be specified AFAICS. The problem is the interpretation of this timeout by some ELs. The spec should be clear that the EL should reply immediately with the best payload it can produce at that moment. There is no reason whatsoever to specify a timeout, but even if people anyway decide to specify it, the EL should anyway reply as fast as it can, and not delay to reply closer to the timeout. In fact I think these bugs are happening **because** the timeout is specified. If we hadn't specified any, ELs would be replying as fast as they can

author: daniellehrner
content: As long as I am a core dev, ELs always tried to build the most valuable block. So we use the time from the timeout to try just that.

author: daniellehrner
content: More time normally translates to more valuable blocks. If that is not what we should do that is fine, we just need to make sure the spec is clear here

author: m.kalinin
content:
```
1. Given the payloadId client software MUST return the most recent version of the payload that is available in the corresponding build process at the time of receiving the call.
```
This is from [here](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/paris.md#specification-2).
So If EL is keep building and doesn't return what is has at the time of the call, this is non-compliance with the existing spec.

Timeout is there to give a room for the time taking to process the call and send back the response. Those timeouts aren't there to allow for extended execution of a method. I guess `getPayload` is the only method that EL would wish to process longer
